transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-29
Time: 14:00 - 14:55 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Martin Reyes (Harborline - Procurement), Leah O'Connor (Harborline - Legal), Diego Alvarez (Harborline - Eng), Asha Menon (Harborline - Security), Samir Rao (Redwood CSM), Nia Brooks (Redwood TPM)

Summary:
Short alignment on procurement lanes, pricing tiers (hosted vs dedicated vs private), DPA/MSA redline timing, KMS/SSO and SOC2 evidence. Customer requested clarity on egress/egress-fee modeling, SLA credits, and an onboarding timeline that fits their Q4 deployment window.

Topics:
- Pricing ladder and committed vs on-demand economics
- Data residency and KMS key ownership (bring-your-own-key)
- DPA redlines and timing for legal review
- Technical preflight for private deployment and connectivity (VPC peering, firewall rules)
- SLA, uptime targets, rollback/fallback behavior and credits

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: okay, thanks everyone for jumping on, um we'll just do quick intros, I'm Alex, AE for Redwood Inference, with Priya on the engineering side.
[00:12] Martin Reyes: Martin here - procurement. we have Leah from legal, Diego and Asha from engineering/security.
[00:18] Priya Patel: hi all. quick note, i'll try to keep the deep tech detail light but happy to drill in.
[00:25] Leah O'Connor: thanks. main agenda from our side is timeline for DPA and MSA review, and clarity on pricing path.
[00:33] Alex Chen: perfect. goal for today: align on the approval lanes - self-serve hosted API path vs dedicated reserved capacity vs private deployment - and agree next steps so procurement and legal can run their tracks.

[00:52] Diego Alvarez: quick question before we start — we run PCI-adjacent workloads. so on KMS: do you support BYOK with HSM integration? or is it vendor-managed keys only?
[01:03] Priya Patel: yes, we do BYOK. in private deployments we can integrate with customer KMS (HSM-backed). hosted also offers a customer-managed key option via cloud KMS, but full HSM attestation is typically in Dedicated or Private installs. there's some nuance there, happy to follow up with security doc.

[01:29] Asha Menon: are audit logs accessible for our auditors? and retention window?
[01:34] Samir Rao: audit logs are available, we have configurable retention — default 90 days on hosted, longer in Dedicated/Private. we can extend retention for enterprise agreements.

[01:47] Martin Reyes: on pricing — procurement wants a simple matrix: committed reserved price, burst pricing, egress/egress-fee, and any pass-through cloud costs. past vendors hid egress as surprises.
[01:59] Alex Chen: totally agree. we'll send a pricing ladder that separates per-token unit cost, reserved GPU seat pricing for Redwood Dedicated, and egress/network pass-through. i'll call out typical egress impact for a high-embedding workload too.

[02:18] Leah O'Connor: on DPA - we need to identify any non-starters. we have standard language for data processing, subprocessors, and deletion timelines. Also: can you confirm your subprocessor list?
[02:29] Priya Patel: we have a maintained subprocessor list + SOC2 attestation. Priya: i'll share the latest subprocessor list, and a SOC2 bridge letter for the private path.

[02:46] Diego Alvarez: one more tech question — does Redwood provide an on-prem package that can be air-gapped? or is private always a VPC-hosted cloud offering?
[02:56] Priya Patel: we have an on-prem option, yes. it's packaged as a private deployment bundle — there are some additional ops requirements for updates. again we'll add the ops checklist.

[03:15] Martin Reyes: timeline wise, procurement wants sign-off before 2027-11-15 to hit our Q4 roadmap. is that realistic?
[03:23] Alex Chen: reasonable. typical runway for customers doing DPA + MSA redlines is 2-4 weeks for initial redline pass, plus procurement/finance sign-off. given holidays, i'd aim to turn initial docs around within one week and then let legal iterate.

[03:40] Leah O'Connor: can you accept some DPA deviations? like subprocessor carve-outs for infra partners? our compliance team may request tighter egress controls.
[03:49] Alex Chen: we try to be pragmatic; there are some standard clauses we can't move on (e.g., liability caps) but for DPA we often accommodate reasonable confidentiality and audit windows. we'll flag must-have clauses.

[04:05] Diego Alvarez: on SLA — what uptime do you commit for Dedicated vs Hosted? and how do credits work?
[04:13] Nia Brooks: for Redwood Dedicated we target 99.9% for model endpoints with a defined incident SLA and credits tied to monthly availability. hosted SLA is lower unless you buy Premium. credits are pro-rata applied to monthly invoice. we can share the SLA grid.

[04:35] Asha Menon: are service degradations logged and traceable per-customer? we need traces for forensics.
[04:42] Priya Patel: yes, we expose per-route traces and request IDs; traces can be exported to your SIEM. again we'll attach the observability docs.

[05:05] Martin Reyes: price pushback — we have internal benchmark against Anthropic and an in-house GPU cluster. procurement priority is cost predictability. do you do committed spend discounts that cascade to tokens and embeddings?
[05:18] Alex Chen: yes — committed monthly spend yields a lowered per-token rate and discounts on dedicated seat pricing. we'll provide tiered examples — 6- and 12-month commitments with breakpoints.

[05:34] Leah O'Connor: egress — what's typical? give a real example, because our finance team will want worst-case scenario for high-embedding churn.
[05:43] Samir Rao: example: if you stream embeddings out at 200TB/month egress, cloud provider egress fees dominate. we show three scenarios in the sheet: low, med, high egress; for many customers embeddings cost more in network than tokens.

[06:02] Diego Alvarez: any auto-fallback if private capacity is exhausted? we'd want app-level graceful degrade to cheaper hosted variant, is that supported?
[06:12] Priya Patel: yes, we support routing policies: prefer private endpoint, fallback to Dedicated or hosted model variant with region and cost controls. that's part of the rollout/traffic policy.

[06:28] Martin Reyes: legal will ask about indemnity and export controls. do you have an export controls annex?
[06:35] Alex Chen: we do have a compliance annex and export controls section in the MSA. we'll surface that.

[06:49] Leah O'Connor: can we get a short readout of the subprocessor list and data flow diagram so we can map to our DPA?
[06:55] Priya Patel: yes — i'll attach the subprocessor list and a simplified dataflow diagram.

[07:06] Alex Chen: quick check — are you leaning toward Dedicated or Private? where does procurement land?
[07:13] Martin Reyes: Need cost predictability and key control, so Private looks best but we need to validate ops burden. Dedicated might be compromise if BYOK for KMS is acceptable.

[07:27] Diego Alvarez: if Dedicated can do our KMS needs and retention windows, we'll evaluate that first. Private is heavier for operations.

[07:35] Alex Chen: got it. we'll outline three recommended lanes in the pricing ladder: Hosted (fast, on-demand), Dedicated (reserved capacity + higher SLA), Private (BYOK, full control, higher ops).

[08:00] Leah O'Connor: DPA redlines — we have a few standard asks: 1) clear subprocessor notification timing; 2) faster data deletion response for deletion requests; 3) audit access for our third-party assessors. any issues with that?
[08:16] Priya Patel: no immediate blockers but need to review specifics. some audit access requests may require an NDA or onsite controls for on-prem/private.

[08:34] Martin Reyes: finance will want a sample invoice and billing cadence. monthly prep or quarterly?
[08:41] Alex Chen: monthly by default; quarterly invoicing available with committed contracts. we'll include sample invoice templates.

[09:02] Diego Alvarez: technical: what are the connectivity options for private? VPC peering, Direct Connect equivalents, or only VPN?
[09:10] Priya Patel: we support VPC peering in major cloud providers, AWS Direct Connect/PrivateLink type options for low-latency, and VPN as fallback. we'll enumerate in the preflight.

[09:33] Asha Menon: encryption in transit — TLS 1.2/1.3 supported? mutual TLS for internal endpoints?
[09:40] Priya Patel: TLS 1.3 and mTLS for private endpoints is supported for mutual auth.

[09:52] Martin Reyes: are there any special clauses for research use? not relevant here but legal always asks.
[09:57] Leah O'Connor: not for us. 

[10:03] Alex Chen: ok i want to pull this together into a single package post-call: 1) pricing ladder and committed examples, 2) SLA grid and sample credits clause, 3) DPA + MSA baseline and subprocessor list, 4) tech preflight runbook for private/dedicated, 5) SOC2 excerpt and network diagram. we'll send those items.

[10:18] Martin Reyes: timeline check — if we get those by early next week, legal can do initial pass and procurement can route for finance.
[10:25] Alex Chen: we'll aim to share docs by EoD Monday (2027-10-04).

[10:35] Leah O'Connor: on liability caps — your standard position?
[10:39] Alex Chen: we have a standard commercial liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months; exceptions are evaluated on an enterprise basis. we'll surface that in the SOW.

[10:55] Diego Alvarez: perf baseline — can you give us a quick sandbox or creds to run a small perf job? we want to compare token latency for our typical payloads.
[11:02] Priya Patel: yes i'll spin up sandbox creds and a short guide. send me Diego's email and i'll provision a 2-week token-limited access.

[11:20] Martin Reyes: one more procurement note: any early-termination fees for reserved capacity?
[11:27] Alex Chen: reserved seats have a ramp and an early-termination schedule; we'll show a 6- and 12-month example and flexibility options.

[11:45] Leah O'Connor: curious about data residency — can you pin data to region EU only?
[11:50] Priya Patel: yes region pinning is supported for private and Dedicated; hosted can be region constrained but may involve additional operational notes. we'll clarify region guarantees.

[12:06] Martin Reyes: ok this is helpful. do you have a recommended next meeting cadence? legal + procurement sync and a technical deep dive with Priya?
[12:15] Alex Chen: recommended: 1) legal redline pass (Leah + Alex) within two weeks, 2) tech deep dive (Priya + Diego) in parallel with sandbox perf (target next week), 3) procurement pricing review (Martin + Alex) after we send pricing ladder.

[12:33] Leah O'Connor: we'll do a redline pass and expect to push back on the subprocessor notification timeframe slightly.

[12:42] Diego Alvarez: i'll take the sandbox and aim to share a perf note by 2027-10-11.

[12:50] Alex Chen: great. final check: any absolute deal-breakers?
[12:55] Asha Menon: long story short, full BYOK + audit access for our compliance team is required for production. if that's not possible we can't go private.
[13:05] Priya Patel: BYOK plus audit logs is available in Private/Dedicated; we'll document exactly how keys are managed and the audit workflow.

[13:18] Martin Reyes: good. recap please?
[13:21] Alex Chen: recap: we'll send a consolidated packet (pricing ladder, SLA grid, DPA baseline, subprocessor list, SOC2 excerpt, private deployment checklist, network diagram) by EoD Monday 2027-10-04. Priya will provision sandbox creds for Diego within 48 hours. Leah will do initial DPA redline and share by 2027-10-08. Customer to confirm SSO/KMS preference by 2027-10-08.

[13:45] Leah O'Connor: thanks everyone. we'll review docs and route internally.
[13:52] Martin Reyes: thanks Alex and team.
[13:55] Alex Chen: thanks all. talk soon.

Action items (restated):
- Alex Chen: pricing ladder, SLA grid, MSA baseline and sample invoice - due 2027-10-04
- Priya Patel: SOC2 excerpt, subprocessor list, dataflow + network diagram, sandbox creding - due 2027-10-06
